stimuli.body:

• Lata occupies March 7.
• Exactly 3 interview slots fall between the interviews of Kiran and Lata.
• Exactly 2 interview slots fall between the interviews of Meera and Hema.
• Exactly 3 interview slots fall between the interviews of Jaya and Meera.

Statements: Only a few loans are branches. All branches are lockers. No lockers is a coins.
Conclusions:
I. Some loans are not branches.
II. No branches is a coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All loans are coins.
II. Some coins are branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All loans are coins.
II. No branches is a coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. Some loans are lockers.
II. Some branches are coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: P = V > S < W > Q.
Conclusions: I. S < V   II. V ≤ S.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
banking rural digital = lu su ka
banking credit access = to su re
rural credit growth = ka vo re
digital access growth = to lu vo
banking rural growth = vo su ka
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: vo. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: banking = su, rural = ka, digital = lu, credit = re, access = to, growth = vo.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 26 km west, turns left and walks 12 km, then turns left and walks 17 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 9 km along the initial direction and 12 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 164 km east, turns right and walks 285 km, then turns right and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 323. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 152 km along the initial direction and 285 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(152² + 285²) = 323 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 133 km south, turns right and walks 240 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: E is the mother of B. C is the daughter of B. G is the father of B. How is C related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. G is a parent of B, and C is B’s daughter. Hence C is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: B is the brother of G. G is the mother of E. C is the father of B and G. How is B related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. B is the brother of E’s mother G. Therefore B is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of C. C is the father of H. B is the son of H. F is the sister of C. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of H, and H is B’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 48 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 25. New front rank = 21+3 = 24. Back rank = 48 − 24 + 1 = 25.

questions.stem: In a queue of 48 candidates, a candidate is 22th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 23. New front rank = 22+4 = 26. Back rank = 48 − 26 + 1 = 23.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2400 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 5381.82. Recover each cost separately: 2400×100/110 + 2400×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 32 and 48 hours. An outlet empties it in 80 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 25.26. Net rate = 1/32 + 1/48 − 1/80 = 19/480 tank/hour. Required time = 25.26 hours.

questions.stem: A boat covers 220 km in still water in 10 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 100. Still-water speed = 22 km/h. Upstream speed = 22 − 2. Distance = speed × 5.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 9:4. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 6 months. A receives ₹108000 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 132000. Profit ratio is 108:24. Each ratio unit = ₹1000. Total = 132 × 1000.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹17000 earns ₹10200 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 24480. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 20%. Compound amount = 17000 × (1 + 20/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 150 litres of pure milk. 30 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain?
questions.explanation: Answer: 96. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 150 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 16 people is 38 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 55. New total minus old total = (16+1)×(38+1) − 16×38 = 55.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 10 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+10)/(x+10) = 3/2 gives x = 10. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 120 m train moving at 97.2 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 5. Relative speed = (97.2 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 24 m/s. Time = 120/24.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 25%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2200. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New quantity / old quantity = 100/125. Reduction percentage = 25/125 ×100.
